label: Arsenate As(V)
description: Shared arsenic exposure anchor linking bacterial arsenate reduction and human arsenic handling.

label: Arsenite As(III)
description: Reduced arsenic species handled through bacterial efflux and human thiol/methylation chemistry.

label: Toluene
description: Shared aromatic hydrocarbon exposure anchor.

label: Benzoate
description: Shared aromatic acid intermediate and human conjugation substrate.

label: Benzoyl-CoA
description: Microbial anaerobic aromatic degradation intermediate; human cells do not use it for respiratory dearomatization.

label: Chromate Cr(VI)
description: Shared metal exposure anchor for microbial extracellular reduction and human intracellular genotoxic reduction.

label: Uranium(VI)
description: Shared radionuclide exposure anchor.

label: Tetrachloroethene PCE
description: Shared organohalide exposure anchor.

label: Trichloroethene TCE
description: Shared chlorinated solvent exposure anchor.

label: Geobacter ArsC/Acr3 arsenic detoxification
description: Bacterial operon-scale arsenate reduction and arsenite efflux module.

label: Human AS3MT/GSH/MRP arsenic handling
description: Human arsenic handling through glutathione complexes, AS3MT methylation, thioredoxin chemistry, and MRP/ABC efflux.

label: Geobacter Bam/Benzoyl-CoA anaerobic aromatics pathway
description: Anaerobic aromatic degradation route that funnels aromatics through benzoyl-CoA and reductive dearomatization.

label: Human CYP2E1 aromatic oxidation
description: Human CYP-mediated oxidation of aromatic solvents such as toluene.

label: Human benzoate glycine conjugation
description: Human detoxification/excretion route converting benzoate to benzoylglycine; capacity depends on glycine and CoA availability.

label: Geobacter extracellular electron transfer metal reduction
description: Microbial extracellular electron-transfer system reducing metals and model oxidants.

label: Human Cr(VI) intracellular reduction and DNA damage
description: Human intracellular Cr(VI) reduction can form Cr(III)-DNA adducts and genotoxic lesions.

label: Geobacter U(VI) to U(IV) biofilm immobilization
description: Microbial biofilm-associated uranium reduction and immobilization.

label: Human uranium nephrotoxicity and metallothionein stress response
description: Human uranium response centered on renal injury, oxidative stress, mitochondrial effects, apoptosis, and metallothionein-associated protection.

label: Geobacter organohalide respiration and dechlorination
description: Geobacter organohalide modules reduce PCE/TCE or chlorinated ethanes under anaerobic conditions.

label: Human TCE/PCE CYP oxidation and GSH conjugation
description: Human TCE/PCE handling through CYP oxidation and glutathione conjugation pathways linked to liver and kidney toxicity.

label: Reduction chemistry
description: Electron-transfer chemistry conserved as a reaction type but not necessarily as a detoxification outcome.

label: Thiol binding and methylation
description: Conserved arsenic chemistry using thiols and methyl transfer.

label: Oxidation and conjugation
description: Human exposure handling shifts many organics toward oxidation and conjugation rather than full catabolic mineralization.

label: Reductive dechlorination
description: Microbial organohalide respiration chemistry absent as an energy metabolism in human cells.

label: Conserved chemistry
description: Same chemical logic retained, often with different proteins or cellular architecture.

label: Analogous function
description: Similar exposure problem handled by non-homologous or differently organized machinery.

label: Pathway loss
description: Microbial pathway absent in human cells.

label: Toxic inversion
description: A transformation that is environmentally detoxifying or respiratory in microbes becomes bioactivating or damaging in human cells.

label: Host-shifted handling
description: Human handling shifts toward distribution, stress response, repair, inflammation, or tissue injury.

label: Cadmium Cd(II)
description: Shared heavy-metal exposure anchor for microbial sorption/transformation and human renal metallothionein stress biology.

label: Mercury Hg(II)
description: Shared mercury exposure anchor for microbial mer detoxification and human GSH/metallothionein renal handling.

label: Methylmercury
description: Neurotoxic organomercury exposure anchor involving thiol and glutathione chemistry.

label: Benzene
description: Aromatic solvent exposure anchor with human bone marrow toxicity and CYP2E1/NQO1-linked susceptibility.

label: Benzo[a]pyrene / PAH
description: Representative PAH exposure anchor for CYP1A1/1B1 activation to DNA-reactive metabolites.

label: 4-Aminobiphenyl
description: Aromatic amine bladder-carcinogen exposure anchor involving CYP/NAT bioactivation and detoxication balance.

label: N-Nitrosodimethylamine NDMA
description: Nitrosamine exposure anchor activated by CYP2E1 to DNA-reactive alkylating species.

label: Aflatoxin B1
description: Hepatocarcinogen exposure anchor activated by CYP enzymes to epoxide metabolites.

label: Acetaldehyde
description: Reactive aldehyde exposure anchor detoxified by ALDH2 but capable of DNA adduct formation.

label: Vinyl chloride
description: Organohalide exposure anchor handled by microbial dechlorination in ecosystems and human bioactivation pathways.

label: 1,2-Dichloroethane
description: Chlorinated ethane exposure anchor with Geobacter strain IAE dihaloelimination evidence.

label: Phenol
description: Phenolic exposure/intermediate represented in Geobacter aromatic degradation and human conjugation/oxidative handling.

label: p-Cresol
description: Methylphenol substrate in Geobacter aromatic metabolism and host/microbial phenolic exposure chemistry.

label: Microbial heavy-metal biosorption and biomineralization
description: General microbial heavy-metal mitigation through biosorption, accumulation, transformation, volatilization, or biomineralization.

label: Microbial mer mercury detoxification
description: Bacterial mercury detoxification logic involving organomercury cleavage and Hg(II) reduction to Hg(0).

label: Human cadmium metallothionein renal toxicity
description: Cadmium accumulates in liver/kidney with metallothionein binding but chronic renal tubular injury and oxidative stress.

label: Human mercury GSH/metallothionein renal-neural handling
description: Mercury handling involves glutathione and metallothionein complexes with renal and neurotoxic consequences.

label: Human methylmercury thiol/GSH neurotoxicity
description: Methylmercury reacts with thiols/selenols, perturbs glutathione homeostasis, and preferentially targets the CNS.

label: Human benzene CYP2E1/NQO1 bone marrow toxicity
description: Benzene metabolism and NQO1-linked susceptibility connect exposure to bone marrow toxicity.

label: Human PAH CYP1A1/1B1 DNA-adduct activation
description: PAHs are activated by CYP1-family enzymes to electrophilic intermediates that form bulky DNA adducts.

label: Human aromatic amine CYP/NAT bladder bioactivation
description: Aromatic amine risk depends on CYP-mediated N-hydroxylation and NAT-mediated detoxication/bioactivation in bladder-relevant tissues.

label: Human nitrosamine CYP2E1 activation and MGMT repair
description: Nitrosamines such as NDMA undergo CYP2E1-dependent activation to DNA alkylating lesions, with MGMT repair relevance.

label: Human aflatoxin CYP epoxidation/GST liver handling
description: Aflatoxin B1 is activated by CYP enzymes to epoxide metabolites with liver cancer relevance and detoxication by GST-related pathways.

label: Human acetaldehyde ALDH2 and esophageal DNA damage
description: ALDH2 protects against acetaldehyde-derived DNA damage, especially in esophageal epithelium.

label: Liver
description: Major human xenobiotic metabolism and first-pass detoxication context.

label: Kidney / renal proximal tubule
description: Renal excretion and metal nephrotoxicity context.

label: Lung
description: Inhalation-exposure and PAH activation context.

label: Bladder urothelium
description: Urinary carcinogen and aromatic amine bioactivation context.

label: Bone marrow / hematopoietic niche
description: Benzene toxicity and hematopoietic susceptibility context.

label: Esophageal epithelium
description: Acetaldehyde DNA-damage and ALDH2 protection context.

label: Central nervous system
description: Methylmercury neurotoxicity context.

label: Ancient catabolic loss
description: Pathway-loss subclass covering catabolic routes reconstructable in early metazoans that have no host-cell equivalent in extant humans.

label: Human-lineage loss
description: Pathway-loss subclass covering pathways lost in Homo sapiens through pseudogenization or fixed loss-of-function variants.

label: Polymorphic loss
description: Pathway-loss subclass covering common loss-of-function or reduced-function polymorphisms that segregate within human populations.

label: Ecosystem-outsourced capacity
description: Capacity absent from human host cells but present in gut/oral/skin microbiome or environmental compartments the host uses.

label: Human FMO3 trimethylamine and tertiary-amine N-oxidation
description: Human FMO3 N-oxidation of trimethylamine, tertiary amines, and organosulfur substrates. Common LoF alleles reduce activity and cause trimethylaminuria.

label: NAT2 slow-acetylator haplotypes
description: NAT2 loss-of-function or reduced-function variant. Polymorphism NAT2*5, *6, *7 slow-acetylator haplotypes. Effect direction reduced_function; effect magnitude severe. gnomAD superpopulation allele frequencies {"AFR":0.42,"AMR":0.45,"EAS":0.15,"EUR":0.55,"SAS":0.42}. Outcome when lost: Reduced N-acetylation of aromatic amines shifts balance toward CYP1A2 N-hydroxylation and DNA-adduct formation. Direct link to 4-aminobiphenyl bladder cancer and PhIP/MeIQx colorectal susceptibility.

label: GSTM1 whole-gene deletion (null)
description: GSTM1 loss-of-function or reduced-function variant. Polymorphism GSTM1*0 whole-gene deletion. Effect direction loss_of_function; effect magnitude null. gnomAD superpopulation allele frequencies {"AFR":0.27,"AMR":0.47,"EAS":0.55,"EUR":0.5,"SAS":0.32}. Outcome when lost: Complete loss of GSTM1 activity reduces glutathione conjugation of benzo[a]pyrene diol epoxide and related PAH metabolites. Elevated lung, bladder, and head-and-neck cancer risk documented in null carriers.

label: GSTT1 whole-gene deletion (null)
description: GSTT1 loss-of-function or reduced-function variant. Polymorphism GSTT1*0 whole-gene deletion. Effect direction loss_of_function; effect magnitude null. gnomAD superpopulation allele frequencies {"AFR":0.25,"AMR":0.2,"EAS":0.55,"EUR":0.2,"SAS":0.15}. Outcome when lost: Complete loss of GSTT1 activity reduces conjugation of small halogenated and epoxide substrates including ethylene oxide, dichloromethane, and vinyl chloride reactive metabolites.

label: UGT1A1*28 promoter TA repeat expansion
description: UGT1A1 loss-of-function or reduced-function variant. Polymorphism UGT1A1*28 A(TA)7TAA promoter repeat. Effect direction reduced_function; effect magnitude moderate. gnomAD superpopulation allele frequencies {"AFR":0.43,"AMR":0.38,"EAS":0.13,"EUR":0.32,"SAS":0.36}. Outcome when lost: TA7 promoter expansion reduces UGT1A1 transcription and glucuronidation of bilirubin, SN-38, and steroid substrates. Gilbert syndrome and irinotecan neutropenia risk.

label: SULT1A1*2 (Arg213His)
description: SULT1A1 loss-of-function or reduced-function variant. Polymorphism SULT1A1*2 c.638G>A p.Arg213His. Effect direction reduced_function; effect magnitude moderate. gnomAD superpopulation allele frequencies {"AFR":0.28,"AMR":0.3,"EAS":0.08,"EUR":0.31,"SAS":0.22}. Outcome when lost: His213 variant reduces heat-stable phenol sulfotransferase activity and thermostability. Affects sulfation of heterocyclic aromatic amines (N-OH-PhIP), tamoxifen, and dietary phenols.

label: NQO1*2 (c.609C>T; null protein)
description: NQO1 loss-of-function or reduced-function variant. Polymorphism NQO1*2 c.609C>T p.Pro187Ser. Effect direction loss_of_function; effect magnitude null. gnomAD superpopulation allele frequencies {"AFR":0.19,"AMR":0.35,"EAS":0.45,"EUR":0.21,"SAS":0.16}. Outcome when lost: Pro187Ser destabilizes NQO1 protein; homozygotes show near-complete loss of two-electron quinone reduction. Increased benzene bone marrow toxicity and altered menadione handling.

label: ALDH2*2 (Glu487Lys)
description: ALDH2 loss-of-function or reduced-function variant. Polymorphism ALDH2*2 c.1510G>A p.Glu487Lys. Effect direction reduced_function; effect magnitude severe. gnomAD superpopulation allele frequencies {"AFR":0.001,"AMR":0.03,"EAS":0.2,"EUR":0.001,"SAS":0.01}. Outcome when lost: Lys487 dominant-negative subunit disrupts tetramer function; heterozygotes retain approximately 6% of activity, homozygotes near zero. Acetaldehyde accumulation on alcohol exposure. Established East Asian esophageal cancer risk factor.

label: CYP2D6*4 splice-defect (poor metabolizer)
description: CYP2D6 loss-of-function or reduced-function variant. Polymorphism CYP2D6*4 c.100C>T + intronic splice. Effect direction loss_of_function; effect magnitude null. gnomAD superpopulation allele frequencies {"AFR":0.06,"AMR":0.11,"EAS":0.01,"EUR":0.2,"SAS":0.11}. Outcome when lost: Splice defect abolishes CYP2D6 activity. Poor-metabolizer phenotype affects handling of tamoxifen, codeine, tricyclics, and xenobiotic substrates. Star-allele diplotype required for accurate calling.

label: FMO3 common LoF haplotype (trimethylaminuria)
description: FMO3 loss-of-function or reduced-function variant. Polymorphism FMO3 c.472G>A + c.769G>A (p.Glu158Lys + p.Val257Met). Effect direction reduced_function; effect magnitude moderate. gnomAD superpopulation allele frequencies {"AFR":0.05,"AMR":0.15,"EAS":0.2,"EUR":0.14,"SAS":0.18}. Outcome when lost: Reduced FMO3 N-oxidation of trimethylamine (from dietary choline, carnitine, betaine) causes trimethylaminuria. Also affects tamoxifen N-oxidation and thiourea/organosulfur handling.

label: GULO (L-gulonolactone oxidase, vitamin C synthesis)
description: Human-lineage loss of GULO / GULOP (pseudogene HGNC:4695). loss_mechanism=pseudogene. Pseudogenized in the haplorrhine ancestor of tarsiers and simian primates approximately 60 million years ago. Three independent inactivating mutations in exons 3 and 11 documented across primates. Also independently lost in guinea pigs and several bat lineages. Exposure-handling consequence: Absolute dietary requirement for vitamin C. Loss of endogenous antioxidant capacity relative to uricase-negative ancestors. Ascorbate serves as the terminal reductant for CYP1A1/1B1 activity and Fenton-chemistry buffering; low ascorbate stress amplifies PAH-related oxidative DNA damage.

label: UOX (urate oxidase / uricase)
description: Human-lineage loss of UOX (pseudogene, human UOX chromosome 1p22). loss_mechanism=pseudogene. Silenced in hominoid ancestor approximately 15 to 20 million years ago via three independent premature-stop-codon mutations followed by regulatory-region decay. Documented in ChimpNet and human pseudogene catalogs. Exposure-handling consequence: Loss of urate oxidation to allantoin. Serum urate elevated 3 to 10-fold relative to uricase-positive mammals. Bridge to gout and to urate-derived reactive oxygen chemistry. Also removed a purine-catabolism sink that some xenobiotic-derived reactive species had used.

label: FMO2 (flavin monooxygenase 2, fixed nonsense variant)
description: Human-lineage loss of FMO2 c.1414C>T p.Q472X (rs6661174). loss_mechanism=fixed_lof_snv. Truncating variant p.Q472X reached near-fixation in non-African populations (approximately 0.98 non-African, approximately 0.75 African). Ancestral functional allele retained in some African populations. Not a pseudogene per HGNC; classic fixed loss-of-function SNV. Exposure-handling consequence: Functional FMO2 N-oxidizes thioureas, aromatic and aliphatic amines including thiobenzamide and 2-aminofluorene. Loss narrows the tissue-level bioactivation profile for thiourea-class xenobiotics and reduces one route of thioamide handling in lung tissue (FMO2 is lung-predominant).

label: HPGD-related prostaglandin catabolism (human-specific reduced expression, candidate)
description: Human-lineage loss of HPGD (15-hydroxyprostaglandin dehydrogenase, tissue-specific expression change). loss_mechanism=expression_loss. Candidate. Human-specific reduction in HPGD expression in colon and lung tissues relative to chimpanzee documented in comparative RNA-seq. Not a pseudogene. Functional consequences for prostaglandin catabolism and inflammation-associated tumor risk are hypothesized but not experimentally resolved. Exposure-handling consequence: Reduced HPGD activity elevates prostaglandin E2 in colon and lung, potentially amplifying inflammation-driven tumor promotion. Candidate mechanism for higher inflammation-associated cancer incidence in humans versus chimpanzee at matched exposures.

label: Gut microbial azoreduction
description: Gut microbial azoreduction. ecological_compartment=gut_microbiome. Representative organisms: Clostridium, Eubacterium, Bacteroides, Enterococcus faecalis, Escherichia coli. Enzymes: azoreductases (AzoR family, NAD(P)H-dependent). Mechanism: Reductive cleavage of aromatic azo bonds (-N=N-) delivering aromatic amines to the enterocyte and portal circulation. Bacterial azoreductases substitute for a capacity absent in mammalian host cells. Antibiotic exposure disrupts the capacity, altering delivered dose to host tissue.

label: Oral microbial nitrate reduction
description: Oral microbial nitrate reduction. ecological_compartment=oral_microbiome. Representative organisms: Veillonella, Actinomyces, Rothia, Prevotella (dorsal-tongue biofilm). Enzymes: bacterial nitrate reductases (nar operon). Mechanism: Salivary glands concentrate dietary nitrate; oral microbes on the tongue dorsum reduce nitrate to nitrite; swallowed nitrite reacts with amines and amides under acid gastric conditions to form N-nitroso compounds. Human cells do not reduce nitrate. Chlorhexidine mouthwash and broad-spectrum antibiotics attenuate the capacity.

label: Gut microbial reductive dehalogenation
description: Gut microbial reductive dehalogenation. ecological_compartment=gut_microbiome. Representative organisms: Dehalobacter, Desulfitobacterium, Clostridium spp., low-abundance gut anaerobes; not all human microbiomes carry it. Enzymes: reductive dehalogenases (rdhA family). Mechanism: Reductive cleavage of C-halogen bonds in small halogenated organics delivered to the gut. Human host cells do not reductively dehalogenate. Capacity depends on the presence of specialized anaerobes and their electron donors. Not universal across human microbiomes.

label: Gut microbial beta-glucuronidase (deconjugation)
identifier: bacterial beta-glucuronidases (gus family, distinct from human GUSB)
description: Gut microbial beta-glucuronidase (deconjugation). ecological_compartment=gut_microbiome. Representative organisms: Bacteroides, Clostridium perfringens, E. coli, and other Firmicutes carrying gus family enzymes. Enzymes: bacterial beta-glucuronidases (gus family, distinct from human GUSB). Mechanism: Microbial beta-glucuronidases hydrolyze host-formed glucuronide conjugates in the gut lumen, releasing aglycones for reabsorption via enterohepatic circulation. Effectively reverses UGT1A1 phase-II inactivation. Directly linked to SN-38 (irinotecan) enterotoxicity and to prolonged systemic exposure to conjugated xenobiotics.

label: AS3MT slow-methylator alleles (M287T + haplotypes)
identifier: AS3MT M287T (rs11191439) plus haplotype tags rs3740393 and rs3740390
description: AS3MT loss-of-function or reduced-function variant. Polymorphism AS3MT c.860T>C p.Met287Thr (rs11191439) and linked haplotypes at rs3740393 and rs3740390. Effect direction reduced_function; effect magnitude moderate. gnomAD superpopulation allele frequencies {"AFR":0.03,"AMR":0.32,"EAS":0.35,"EUR":0.10,"SAS":0.14}. Outcome when lost: reduced conversion of monomethylarsonic acid (MMA) to dimethylarsinic acid (DMA); elevated urinary %MMA is the standard biomarker. Increased risk of arsenic-associated skin, bladder, and lung cancer in high-exposure populations (Bangladesh, Chile, Argentina, Taiwan). Also linked to gestational exposure outcomes.

label: Dehalococcoides complete dechlorination to ethene
description: Dehalococcoides mccartyi 195 catalyzes complete PCE/TCE reductive dechlorination all the way to non-toxic ethene, unlike Geobacter which stalls at cis-DCE. Reference for the ancient_catabolic subclass in the organohalide pathway.

label: KT2440 aerobic aromatic-amine oxidation
description: Aerobic bacterial oxidation of aromatic amines via dedicated amine oxidases; a catabolic route absent from human host cells, which instead use NAT2 acetylation (polymorphic) or CYP1A2 N-hydroxylation (bioactivation). Provides the ancient_catabolic column for the 4-aminobiphenyl case study.

label: KT2440 PAH ring-hydroxylation (aerobic)
description: Aerobic bacterial ring-hydroxylating dioxygenase attack on PAHs including benzo[a]pyrene, producing cis-dihydrodiols instead of the arene-oxide + trans-dihydrodiol products that drive mammalian PAH bioactivation. Provides the ancient_catabolic column for the benzo[a]pyrene case study.

label: R. erythropolis F420-dependent AFB1 reduction
description: F420-dependent oxidoreductase family catalyzes reductive detoxification of aflatoxin B1 in R. erythropolis and related actinomycetes; a bacterial catabolic route absent from human hepatocytes, which instead generate the mutagenic exo-8,9-epoxide via CYP1A2/3A4.

label: Rhodococcus sp. ANM-7 aerobic NDMA degradation
description: Aerobic propane-monooxygenase-mediated NDMA degradation in Rhodococcus sp. ANM-7; a catabolic route absent from human hepatocytes, which instead bioactivate NDMA via CYP2E1.

label: B. thetaiotaomicron azoreductase (aromatic amine release)
description: FMN-dependent gut azoreductase reductively cleaves azo-linked aromatic-amine precursors, releasing free 4-aminobiphenyl and related aromatic amines back into the lumen. Ecosystem_outsourced activity that modulates the effective 4-ABP dose the human host must handle via CYP1A2/NAT2.

label: B. thetaiotaomicron beta-glucuronidase (AFB1 deconjugation)
description: Gut beta-glucuronidase deconjugates host-glucuronidated aflatoxin metabolites in the intestinal lumen, releasing free AFB1 for reabsorption. Ecosystem_outsourced activity that opposes host UGT detoxification.

label: V. parvula oral nitrate reduction (entero-salivary cycle)
description: Oral commensal periplasmic nitrate reduction (Napa-type) is the canonical driver of the entero-salivary nitrate cycle. Feeds nitrite to the acidic stomach where N-nitrosation reactions may generate nitrosamines. Ecosystem_outsourced activity that shapes endogenous nitrosamine formation.
